answer: In a market where agents trade yarrow, orchard fruit, and falcon tracking data, governance votes are weighted by collateral locked for 30 days, not by account count. Each unit of collateral can back only one account at a time, so dividing a deposit among a thousand fake identities creates no extra voting power. To gain influence, an attacker must buy and immobilize more collateral, bearing its financing cost and price risk throughout the lockup.
